title: Overnight contingency log and action anchors — Dec 02 2027
summary: Short recap of the overnight watch window where we saw a cross-region cache degradation that increased tail latency on hosted API read paths. Primary impact window: 2027-12-02 02:10–03:25 UTC. No customer-facing downtime, degraded 95/99th latencies and elevated 5xxs on embedding endpoints during spike. Root cause appears related to concurrent eviction storms on Redis replicas after a maintenance job overlapped with background compaction on storage nodes.
timeline_and_actions:
02:05 UTC — Alert: increased 5xx rate and host latency from embedding route (monitoring alert: embed-5xx-rate-high).
02:10 UTC — Full alert page posted to #sre-ops; PagerDuty P123 triggered.
02:12 UTC — First responder (Priya) verified graphs, correlated with redis replica CPU and eviction counters.
02:20 UTC — Scoped to cache layer: redis-replica-3 showing high evicted-keys, OOM-like churn (no OOM kill).
02:25 UTC — Mitigation: rolled traffic for embedding-read->fallback to LRU-cache-layer (temporary routing via runtime flag). Immediate 30% drop in 5xx.
02:34 UTC — Eng infra (Miles) increased redis-replica pool size on eu-west with 2x memory buffer for 20 minutes to stop eviction cascade.
02:50 UTC — Observed stabilization of evictions; latency returning to baseline for P50/P90, but P99 remained elevated.
03:05 UTC — Root-cause hypothesis refined: maintenance compaction job on storage nodes saturated IO; background eviction + compaction amplified memory pressure on redis replicas that share host.
03:15 UTC — Decided not to perform disruptive restarts; kept temporary routing and increased replica sizing.
03:25 UTC — Primary alerts suppressed; pager duty incident transitioned to follow-up ticket SRE-3217.
03:30 UTC — Watch transfer to day team (Aisha) with notes and follow-ups.
observations_and_debug_notes:
- Eviction spikes correlate with storage compaction windows (see infra logs /var/log/compaction).
- Autoscaler flapped briefly when replica CPU trend crossed threshold; short TTL on scale down caused thrashing.
- No evidence of application-level memory leak; metrics indicate transient pressure.
- Redis persistence (AOF) not the driver; AOF rewrite jobs were idle at the time.
- A few nodes in the eu-west pool reported high iowait (~45%) during the window.
runbook_updates_requested:
1) Add a dedicated section to the cache-failover runbook for eviction-storm symptom checklist: eviction counters, iowait, compaction jobs, and routing flags. (owner: Jonas, ticket: SRE-3218).
2) Increase autoscaler downscale grace window for redis-replicas from 60s to 180s to prevent immediate scale-down thrash. (owner: Miles, PR: infra#842).
3) Add an observability panel that shows compaction job schedules vs eviction rate (owner: Aisha).
4) Document the temporary routing flag (runtime.fallback.embed_reads) with exact toggle steps and rollback guidance.
follow_ups_and_owners:
- SRE-3217 (post-incident follow-up): full RCA draft and timeline (owner: Priya).
- SRE-3218 (runbook edits): add eviction-storm checklist and diagrams (owner: Jonas).
- infra#842 (autoscaler change): PR created, needs review and canary (owner: Miles).
- Observability card: add compaction vs eviction panels to SLI dashboard (owner: Aisha).
- Ops drill: schedule a tabletop for cache failover flows in next on-call training (owner: eng-sre).
open_questions_and_risks:
- Why did storage compaction overlap with maintenance job? Need to confirm scheduler behavior for compaction windows.
- Is there any collocated workload pattern that makes redis hosts susceptible to IO interference? Consider isolating persistent compaction workloads to dedicated hosts.
- Risk: the runtime fallback flag is effective but reduces cache hit rate and increases tokens served on host; long-term use increases cost. Need an SLA-equivalent trigger for automated fallback.
notes_for_next_watch:
- If alert triggers again: first action = check eviction counters and iowait before cycling nodes. Avoid restarts unless eviction counters continue to rise after memory buffer increase.
- Keep fallback flag documented and accessible in runtime/flags with an audit trail.
- Runbook quick link: Confluence:runbooks/cache-failover (we need to update).
quick_commands_snapshot:
(for SRE responders)
# check eviction metrics
kubectl -n infra exec -it redis-replica-3 -- redis-cli info stats | grep evicted
# check iowait on host
ssh ops@host-xyz 'cat /proc/stat | grep iowait'
# increase replica class (k8s HPA)
kubectl -n infra scale deployment/redis-replica --replicas=6
closing_remarks:
Good containment overnight — playbook actions and temporary routing prevented customer-visible outages. Biggest gap: runbook lacked a specific eviction-storm troubleshooting path and autoscaler grace settings need hardening. Recommended priority: SRE-3218 + infra#842 review in next 48 hours.

Transferred to day team (Aisha) for morning follow-ups. Logged updates in the incident tracker and created follow-up tickets.
